Assertion records

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge chartography · human annotation: Chartography tasks are authored by working domain professionals with a target answer and a complete walkthrough of the visual readings and calculations; for visually estimated quantities, authors provide a chart-specific acceptable range. Each task is independently checked by three additional domain experts and retained only if screening elicits a meaningful failure in at least one frontier model.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.chartography.construction.v3

Start a public GitHub correction · GitHub requires sign-in.

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Eleven US native-English adult participants produce 200 conversations with eight anonymized original models. Diagnostic data are self-reported; conversations are not independent participants.
  • GPT-4o-mini suggests question subsets that participants may revise. Golden responses are participant-edited after viewing original and preference-informed model outputs, rather than independent wholly human-written references.
  • Eleven evaluation models predict participant annotations. Default does not use future turns; Omniscient includes privileged profiles. Mistral Large draft scores and Kendall tau are supplementary and excluded from the Composite.
  • Pooled tests assume conversation independence despite repeated participants. Conversation-level Pearson r=-0.097 and model-level Spearman rho=-0.36 have different statistical units and are not interchangeable.
  • The human baseline has three raters and seven conversations. Small imbalanced culturally restricted samples and self-report limit interpretation; the authors explicitly exclude clinical validation and safety-critical deployment use.

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Experts adapt ten industry handbooks into 65 fictional-company tasks with per-task operative policy mutations. Handbooks span 20-124 rendered pages and arrive as PDF, Word or HTML.
  • Eight hundred twenty-four deterministic Python criteria check final workspace/service state, including required outputs and prohibited behavior. No LLM judging is used; strict pass requires all criteria, with four trials per task and a separate N-minus-one metric.
  • Task builders iterate tasks and criteria against repeated model runs. A common OpenHands harness caps each trial at 200 tool calls and one hour; provider/transport errors are excluded and rerun.
  • July Table 2 has thirty configurations, while the cost/efficiency section refers to twenty configurations evaluated at release. Strict and relaxed metrics remain separate.
  • Industry-policy inspiration and mock services do not constitute observation of actual private corporate work or an independent audit of pretraining contamination or deployment safety.
